result.summary: Deprecates the `replaceable` argument in transaction and PSBT creation and modification RPCs, including `createrawtransaction`, `fundrawtransaction`, `createpsbt`, `walletcreatefundedpsbt`, `send`, `sendtoaddress`, `sendmany`, `sendall`, `bumpfee`, and `psbtbumpfee`. Supplying this argument now raises an `RPC_METHOD_DEPRECATED` error unless Bitcoin Core is started with `-deprecatedrpc=bip125`. Functional tests and release notes are updated accordingly.
result.problem: With full-RBF being the default mempool replacement policy network-wide since Bitcoin Core v28, transactions are replaceable by fee regardless of BIP 125 opt-in sequence signalling. Maintaining RPC parameters that toggle opt-in signalling adds redundant API surface and code complexity.
evidence: PR description: 'This builds upon the existing issue of removing the option for users to signal replaceability because fullrbf is the default policy and prevalent in the network (since bitcoin core v28 was released in late 2024) that makes every transaction replaceable by default, making this user option unnecessary.'
Fixes linked issue #32661 ('wallet, node: Redundant opt-in RBF wallet config and RPC parameters').

enables: Complete removal of the `replaceable` RPC argument and associated opt-in RBF sequencing logic in a future major release.

result.scope_notes: Touches 10 RPC commands across wallet and node RPC endpoints (`rawtransaction.cpp` and `wallet/rpc/spend.cpp`), and updates test fixtures across several functional tests to remove legacy `replaceable` arguments.
result.card: Deprecates the `replaceable` parameter across transaction and PSBT creation and modification RPCs, requiring `-deprecatedrpc=bip125` to continue passing it. Because full-RBF has been enabled by default across the network since Bitcoin Core v28, opt-in BIP 125 signalling is redundant, leaving lingering API complexity. This addresses issue #32661 as part of a wider effort to retire obsolete opt-in RBF options.
